blocks.text: Blob World refers to the wave of graphic design that emerged in the mid-2010s. It utilizes 3D renders to create blobby proportions, gelatinous, curvy organic shapes, translucent, glossy, strange and mixes playful textures with fluid, bizarre, and sometimes unsettling body-horror compositions.
Blob World uses 3D graphics to create surreal and sometimes unnerving imagery with playful textures and uncanny forms. Matte and glossy shaders are used to replicate clay, rubber, plastic, or glass.
abstract landscapes incorporating floating rings, checkerboard floors, or minimalist architecture.
dreamy pastels, saturated gradients, and neon highlights to foster a cheerful but surreal mood.
Surfaces alternate between matte rubber, ultra-glossy jelly finishes, or tactile, strange ridges.
Heavy usage of stretching, melting and inflating 3D structures that replicate clay, bubbly, wooly, or soft plastic.
Physical Products: Chunky resin homeware, curvy "squiggle" mirrors, and wavy pastel furniture that often bring the digital trend into interior spaces.
Limbless, stylized, or hyper-flexible figures popularized by prominent artists such as Jack Sachs.
